A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
allergic asthma is caused by a dysregulated immune response to inhaled antigens.

The main takeaway from our work is that
asthma results from the dysregulation of immune responses to allergen, and the dysregulation is not restricted to the airways.

the immune response to inhaled allergen is not simply a Th2 response to a single antigen, but rather a dysregulated response to a complex mixture of allergens, which results in the production of a wide variety of cytokines and chemokines, as well as a number of effector cells.

the immune response to allergens is not a simple Th2 versus Th1 paradigm, but rather a complex interplay of Th2 cells, T regulatory cells, Th1 cells, Th17 cells, and innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) in which the relative balance between these cell populations determines the nature of the immune response to inhaled antigens.
